data.narrative:
AlixLabs is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Jonas Sundqvist, Dmitry Suyatin, and Amin Karimi, with €15M in total capital raised to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes a peer universe of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies, though narrow stage-matched peers are sparse.

Given data constraints, only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-Progression analysis uses the €15M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding €30M. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be deployed without disclosed revenue; while the Semiconductors peer set shows a 21.4x P/S median across the three public tickers, this metric is not actionable here. Peer-Median analysis is similarly inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting minimum thresholds (the sector contains 12 total peers, but only 1-2 qualify per filter).

The analysis supports a valuation range of €26M to €34M, centered on €30M. This range reflects modest upside from capital deployed, consistent with early-stage risk in semiconductor R&D. Key uncertainties include the target's current burn rate, technical differentiation relative to named peers (SambaNova, Cerebras, Etched, PsiQuantum, Credo), and path to revenue inflection. Revenue disclosure or detailed technical IP assessment would substantially narrow the range.
